Return the IDs of all lines belonging to the printed abstract in reading order, including continuations across columns or pages. Within a PDF page, larger y is higher on the page.
Exclude the abstract heading, affiliations, keywords, introduction, conference notices, footnotes, running headers and page numbers. Omit any unrelated line even if it interrupts the abstract in the supplied order.
For an inline heading or unrelated text at the boundary, put the exact prefix of the first selected line to omit in skipStart, and the exact suffix of the last selected line to omit in skipEnd. Otherwise use empty strings. If you cannot locate the printed abstract, return an empty lines array.
Also locate the full body of the paper across all supplied pages, including the appendix. In body, return inclusive first/last line ID ranges in reading order. Each range is one contiguous run of PDF lines on a single page. Use separate ranges for separated text on a page. Include section headings and substantive prose. Exclude the abstract, title and author material, running headers, page numbers and bibliography. Retain all eligible body prose, including results and limitations.

{"title":"Attention Is All You Need","arxivAbstract":"The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks in an encoder-decoder configuration. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature. We show that the Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.","pdfLines":["1 [p1 x125 y710 s12] Provided proper attribution is provided, Google hereby grants permission to","2 [p1 x124 y696 s12] reproduce the tables and figures in this paper solely for use in journalistic or","3 [p1 x268 y682 s12] scholarly works.","4 [p1 x211 y630 s17] Attention Is All You Need","5 [p1 x133 y549 s10] Ashish Vaswani∗","6 [p1 x139 y538 s10] Google Brain","7 [p1 x117 y527 s10] avaswani@google.com","8 [p1 x239 y549 s10] Noam Shazeer∗","9 [p1 x243 y538 s10] Google Brain","10 [p1 x231 y527 s10] noam@google.com","11 [p1 x339 y549 s10] Niki Parmar∗","12 [p1 x331 y538 s10] Google Research","13 [p1 x324 y527 s10] nikip@google.com","14 [p1 x424 y549 s10] Jakob Uszkoreit∗","15 [p1 x425 y538 s10] Google Research","16 [p1 x422 y527 s10] usz@google.com","17 [p1 x144 y499 s10] Llion Jones∗","18 [p1 x135 y488 s10] Google Research","19 [p1 x127 y477 s10] llion@google.com","20 [p1 x249 y499 s10] Aidan N. Numerous","60 [p2 x108 y653 s10] efforts have since continued to push the boundaries of recurrent language models and encoder-decoder","61 [p2 x108 y642 s10] architectures [38, 24, 15].","62 [p2 x108 y625 s10] Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and output","63 [p2 x108 y614 s10] sequences. Aligning the positions to steps in computation time, they generate a sequence of hidden","64 [p2 x108 y604 s10] states ht, as a function of the previous hidden state ht−1 and the input for position t. This inherently","65 [p2 x108 y593 s10] sequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longer","66 [p2 x108 y582 s10] sequence lengths, as memory constraints limit batching across examples. Recent work has achieved","67 [p2 x108 y571 s10] significant improvements in computational efficiency through factorization tricks [21] and conditional","68 [p2 x108 y560 s10] computation [32], while also improving model performance in case of the latter. The fundamental","69 [p2 x108 y549 s10] constraint of sequential computation, however, remains.","70 [p2 x108 y533 s10] Attention mechanisms have become an integral part of compelling sequence modeling and transduc-","71 [p2 x108 y522 s10] tion models in various tasks, allowing modeling of dependencies without regard to their distance in","72 [p2 x108 y511 s10] the input or output sequences [2, 19]. In all but a few cases [27], however, such attention mechanisms","73 [p2 x108 y500 s10] are used in conjunction with a recurrent network.","74 [p2 x108 y483 s10] In this work we propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and instead","75 [p2 x108 y473 s10] relying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.","76 [p2 x108 y462 s10] The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art in","77 [p2 x108 y451 s10] translation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.","78 [p2 x108 y420 s12] 2 Background","79 [p2 x108 y395 s10] The goal of reducing sequential computation also forms the foundation of the Extended Neural GPU","80 [p2 x108 y384 s10] [16], ByteNet [18] and ConvS2S [9], all of which use convolutional neural networks as basic building","81 [p2 x108 y373 s10] block, computing hidden representations in parallel for all input and output positions. In these models,","82 [p2 x108 y362 s10] the number of operations required to relate signals from two arbitrary input or output positions grows","83 [p2 x108 y351 s10] in the distance between positions, linearly for ConvS2S and logarithmically for ByteNet. This makes","84 [p2 x108 y340 s10] it more difficult to learn dependencies between distant positions [12]. In the Transformer this is","85 [p2 x108 y330 s10] reduced to a constant number of operations, albeit at the cost of reduced effective resolution due","86 [p2 x108 y319 s10] to averaging attention-weighted positions, an effect we counteract with Multi-Head Attention as","87 [p2 x108 y308 s10] described in section 3.2.","88 [p2 x108 y291 s10] Self-attention, sometimes called intra-attention is an attention mechanism relating different positions","89 [p2 x108 y280 s10] of a single sequence in order to compute a representation of the sequence. Self-attention has been","90 [p2 x108 y270 s10] used successfully in a variety of tasks including reading comprehension, abstractive summarization,","91 [p2 x108 y259 s10] textual entailment and learning task-independent sentence representations [4, 27, 28, 22].","92 [p2 x108 y242 s10] End-to-end memory networks are based on a recurrent attention mechanism instead of sequence-","93 [p2 x108 y231 s10] aligned recurrence and have been shown to perform well on simple-language question answering and","94 [p2 x108 y220 s10] language modeling tasks [34].","95 [p2 x108 y204 s10] To the best of our knowledge, however, the Transformer is the first transduction model relying","96 [p2 x108 y193 s10] entirely on self-attention to compute representations of its input and output without using sequence-","97 [p2 x108 y182 s10] aligned RNNs or convolution. In the following sections, we will describe the Transformer, motivate","98 [p2 x108 y171 s10] self-attention and discuss its advantages over models such as [17, 18] and [9].","99 [p2 x108 y140 s12] 3 Model Architecture","100 [p2 x108 y116 s10] Most competitive neural sequence transduction models have an encoder-decoder structure [5, 2, 35].","101 [p2 x108 y105 s10] Here, the encoder maps an input sequence of symbol representations (x1, ..., xn) to a sequence","102 [p2 x108 y94 s10] of continuous representations z = (z1, ..., zn). Given z, the decoder then generates an output","103 [p2 x108 y83 s10] sequence (y1, ..., ym) of symbols one element at a time. At each step the model is auto-regressive","104 [p2 x108 y72 s10] [10], consuming the previously generated symbols as additional input when generating the next.","105 [p2 x304 y42 s10] 2","106 [p3 x210 y380 s10] Figure 1: The Transformer - model architecture.","107 [p3 x108 y348 s10] The Transformer follows this overall architecture using stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully","108 [p3 x108 y337 s10] connected layers for both the encoder and decoder, shown in the left and right halves of Figure 1,","109 [p3 x108 y326 s10] respectively.","110 [p3 x108 y301 s10] 3.1 Encoder and Decoder Stacks","111 [p3 x108 y281 s10] Encoder: The encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers. Each layer has two","112 [p3 x108 y270 s10] sub-layers. The first is a multi-head self-attention mechanism, and the second is a simple, position-","113 [p3 x108 y260 s10] wise fully connected feed-forward network. We employ a residual connection [11] around each of","114 [p3 x108 y249 s10] the two sub-layers, followed by layer normalization [1]. That is, the output of each sub-layer is","115 [p3 x108 y238 s10] LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x)), where Sublayer(x) is the function implemented by the sub-layer","116 [p3 x108 y227 s10] itself. To facilitate these residual connections, all sub-layers in the model, as well as the embedding","117 [p3 x108 y216 s10] layers, produce outputs of dimension dmodel = 512.","118 [p3 x108 y193 s10] Decoder: The decoder is also composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers. In addition to the two","119 [p3 x108 y182 s10] sub-layers in each encoder layer, the decoder inserts a third sub-layer, which performs multi-head","120 [p3 x108 y171 s10] attention over the output of the encoder stack. Similar to the encoder, we employ residual connections","121 [p3 x108 y160 s10] around each of the sub-layers, followed by layer normalization. We also modify the self-attention","122 [p3 x108 y149 s10] sub-layer in the decoder stack to prevent positions from attending to subsequent positions. This","123 [p3 x108 y138 s10] masking, combined with fact that the output embeddings are offset by one position, ensures that the","124 [p3 x108 y127 s10] predictions for position i can depend only on the known outputs at positions less than i.","125 [p3 x108 y103 s10] 3.2 Attention","126 [p3 x108 y83 s10] An attention function can be described as mapping a query and a set of key-value pairs to an output,","127 [p3 x108 y72 s10] where the query, keys, values, and output are all vectors. The input consists of","136 [p4 x108 y404 s10] queries and keys of dimension dk, and values of dimension dv . We compute the dot products of the","137 [p4 x108 y393 s10] query with all keys, divide each by √dk, and apply a softmax function to obtain the weights on the","138 [p4 x108 y382 s10] values.","139 [p4 x108 y366 s10] In practice, we compute the attention function on a set of queries simultaneously, packed together","140 [p4 x108 y355 s10] into a matrix Q. The keys and values are also packed together into matrices K and V . Dot-product attention is identical to our algorithm, except for the scaling factor","147 [p4 x108 y263 s10] of 1√dk","148 [p4 x136 y263 s10] . Additive attention computes the compatibility function using a feed-forward network with","149 [p4 x108 y250 s10] a single hidden layer. While the two are similar in theoretical complexity, dot-product attention is","150 [p4 x108 y239 s10] much faster and more space-efficient in practice, since it can be implemented using highly optimized","151 [p4 x108 y228 s10] matrix multiplication code.","152 [p4 x108 y212 s10] While for small values of dk the two mechanisms perform similarly, additive attention outperforms","153 [p4 x108 y201 s10] dot product attention without scaling for larger values of dk [3]. We suspect that for large values of","154 [p4 x108 y190 s10] dk, the dot products grow large in magnitude, pushing the softmax function into regions where it has","155 [p4 x108 y179 s10] extremely small gradients 4. To counteract this effect, we scale the dot products by 1√dk","156 [p4 x457 y179 s10] .","157 [p4 x108 y154 s10] 3.2.2 Multi-Head Attention","158 [p4 x108 y135 s10] Instead of performing a single attention function with dmodel-dimensional keys, values and queries,","159 [p4 x108 y124 s10] we found it beneficial to linearly project the queries, keys and values h times with different, learned","160 [p4 x108 y113 s10] linear projections to dk, dk and dv dimensions, respectively. These are concatenated and once again projected, resulting in the final values, as","167 [p5 x108 y699 s10] depicted in Figure 2.","168 [p5 x108 y683 s10] Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation","169 [p5 x108 y672 s10] subspaces at different positions. For each of these we use","181 [p5 x108 y539 s10] dk = dv = dmodel/h = 64. Due to the reduced dimension of each head, the total computational cost","182 [p5 x108 y528 s10] is similar to that of single-head attention with full dimensionality.","183 [p5 x108 y504 s10] 3.2.3 Applications of Attention in our Model","184 [p5 x108 y485 s10] The Transformer uses multi-head attention in three different ways:","185 [p5 x135 y464 s10] • In \"encoder-decoder attention\" layers, the queries come from the previous decoder layer,","186 [p5 x144 y453 s10] and the memory keys and values come from the output of the encoder. This allows every","187 [p5 x144 y442 s10] position in the decoder to attend over all positions in the input sequence. This mimics the","188 [p5 x144 y431 s10] typical encoder-decoder attention mechanisms in sequence-to-sequence models such as","189 [p5 x144 y421 s10] [38, 2, 9].","190 [p5 x135 y405 s10] • The encoder contains self-attention layers. In a self-attention layer all of the keys, values","191 [p5 x144 y394 s10] and queries come from the same place, in this case, the output of the previous layer in the","192 [p5 x144 y383 s10] encoder. Each position in the encoder can attend to all positions in the previous layer of the","193 [p5 x144 y372 s10] encoder.","194 [p5 x135 y356 s10] • Similarly, self-attention layers in the decoder allow each position in the decoder to attend to","195 [p5 x144 y345 s10] all positions in the decoder up to and including that position. We need to prevent leftward","196 [p5 x144 y334 s10] information flow in the decoder to preserve the auto-regressive property. We implement this","197 [p5 x144 y323 s10] inside of scaled dot-product attention by masking out (setting to −∞) all values in the input","198 [p5 x144 y313 s10] of the softmax which correspond to illegal connections. See Figure 2.","199 [p5 x108 y287 s10] 3.3 Position-wise Feed-Forward Networks","200 [p5 x108 y267 s10] In addition to attention sub-layers, each of the layers in our encoder and decoder contains a fully","201 [p5 x108 y256 s10] connected feed-forward network, which is applied to each position separately and identically. This","202 [p5 x108 y245 s10] consists of two linear transformations with a ReLU activation in between.","203 [p5 x227 y216 s10] FFN(x) = max(0, xW1 + b1)W2 + b2 (2)","204 [p5 x108 y194 s10] While the linear transformations are the same across different positions, they use different parameters","205 [p5 x108 y183 s10] from layer to layer. Another way of describing this is as two convolutions with kernel size 1.","206 [p5 x108 y172 s10] The dimensionality of input and output is dmodel = 512, and the inner-layer has dimensionality","207 [p5 x108 y162 s10] df f = 2048.","208 [p5 x108 y136 s10] 3.4 Embeddings and Softmax","209 [p5 x108 y116 s10] Similarly to other sequence transduction models, we use learned embeddings to convert the input","210 [p5 x108 y105 s10] tokens and output tokens to vectors of dimension dmodel. We also use the usual learned linear transfor-","211 [p5 x108 y94 s10] mation and softmax function to convert the decoder output to predicted next-token probabilities. In","212 [p5 x108 y83 s10] our model, we share the same weight matrix between the two embedding layers and the pre-softmax","213 [p5 x108 y72 s10] linear transformation, similar to [30]. In the embedding layers, we multiply those weights by √dmodel.","214 [p5 x304 y42 s10] 5","215 [p6 x108 y713 s10] Table 1: Maximum path lengths, per-layer complexity and minimum number of sequential operations","216 [p6 x108 y702 s10] for different layer types. n is the sequence length, d is the representation dimension, k is the kernel","217 [p6 x108 y691 s10] size of convolutions and r the size of the neighborhood in restricted self-attention.","218 [p6 x125 y668 s10] Layer Type Complexity per Layer Sequential Maximum Path Length","219 [p6 x339 y657 s10] Operations","220 [p6 x125 y644 s10] Self-Attention O(n2 · d) O(1) O(1)","221 [p6 x125 y633 s10] Recurrent O(n · d2) O(n) O(n)","222 [p6 x125 y621 s10] Convolutional O(k · n · d2) O(1) O(logk(n))","223 [p6 x125 y611 s10] Self-Attention (restricted) O(r · n · d) O(1) O(n/r)","224 [p6 x108 y571 s10] 3.5 Positional Encoding","225 [p6 x108 y551 s10] Since our model contains no recurrence and no convolution, in order for the model to make use of the","226 [p6 x108 y540 s10] order of the sequence, we must inject some information about the relative or absolute position of the","227 [p6 x108 y529 s10] tokens in the sequence. To this end, we add \"positional encodings\" to the input embeddings at the","228 [p6 x108 y518 s10] bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks. The positional encodings have the same dimension dmodel","229 [p6 x108 y507 s10] as the embeddings, so that the two can be summed. There are many choices of positional encodings,","230 [p6 x108 y496 s10] learned and fixed [9].","231 [p6 x108 y480 s10] In this work, we use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies:","232 [p6 x236 y446 s10] P E(pos,2i) = sin(pos/100002i/dmodel )","233 [p6 x226 y429 s10] P E(pos,2i+1) = cos(pos/100002i/dmodel )","234 [p6 x108 y407 s10] where pos is the position and i is the dimension. That is, each dimension of the positional encoding","235 [p6 x108 y396 s10] corresponds to a sinusoid. The wavelengths form a geometric progression from 2π to 10000 · 2π. We","236 [p6 x108 y385 s10] chose this function because we hypothesized it would allow the model to easily learn to attend by","237 [p6 x108 y374 s10] relative positions, since for any fixed offset k, P Epos+k can be represented as a linear function of","238 [p6 x108 y363 s10] P Epos.","239 [p6 x108 y347 s10] We also experimented with using learned positional embeddings [9] instead, and found that the two","240 [p6 x108 y336 s10] versions produced nearly identical results (see Table 3 row (E)). We chose the sinusoidal version","241 [p6 x108 y325 s10] because it may allow the model to extrapolate to sequence lengths longer than the ones encountered","242 [p6 x108 y314 s10] during training.","243 [p6 x108 y286 s12] 4 Why Self-Attention","244 [p6 x108 y263 s10] In this section we compare various aspects of self-attention layers to the recurrent and convolu-","245 [p6 x108 y252 s10] tional layers commonly used for mapping one variable-length sequence of symbol representations","246 [p6 x107 y241 s10] (x1, ..., xn) to another sequence of equal length (z1, ..., zn), with xi, zi ∈ Rd, such as a hidden","247 [p6 x108 y230 s10] layer in a typical sequence transduction encoder or decoder. Motivating our use of self-attention we","248 [p6 x108 y219 s10] consider three desiderata.","249 [p6 x108 y203 s10] One is the total computational complexity per layer. Another is the amount of computation that can","250 [p6 x108 y192 s10] be parallelized, as measured by the minimum number of sequential operations required.","251 [p6 x108 y176 s10] The third is the path length between long-range dependencies in the network. Learning long-range","252 [p6 x108 y165 s10] dependencies is a key challenge in many sequence transduction tasks. One key factor affecting the","253 [p6 x108 y154 s10] ability to learn such dependencies is the length of the paths forward and backward signals have to","254 [p6 x108 y143 s10] traverse in the network. The shorter these paths between any combination of positions in the input","255 [p6 x108 y132 s10] and output sequences, the easier it is to learn long-range dependencies [12]. Hence we also compare","256 [p6 x108 y121 s10] the maximum path length between any two input and output positions in networks composed of the","257 [p6 x108 y110 s10] different layer types.","258 [p6 x108 y94 s10] As noted in Table 1, a self-attention layer connects all positions with a constant number of sequentially","259 [p6 x108 y83 s10] executed operations, whereas a recurrent layer requires O(n) sequential operations. In terms of","260 [p6 x108 y72 s10] computational complexity, self-attention layers are faster than recurrent layers when the sequence","261 [p6 x304 y42 s10] 6","262 [p7 x108 y710 s10] length n is smaller than the representation dimensionality d, which is most often the case with","263 [p7 x108 y699 s10] sentence representations used by state-of-the-art models in machine translations, such as word-piece","264 [p7 x108 y688 s10] [38] and byte-pair [31] representations. To improve computational performance for tasks involving","265 [p7 x108 y677 s10] very long sequences, self-attention could be restricted to considering only a neighborhood of size r in","266 [p7 x108 y666 s10] the input sequence centered around the respective output position. This would increase the maximum","267 [p7 x108 y655 s10] path length to O(n/r). We plan to investigate this approach further in future work.","268 [p7 x108 y639 s10] A single convolutional layer with kernel width k < n does not connect all pairs of input and output","269 [p7 x108 y628 s10] positions. Doing so requires a stack of O(n/k) convolutional layers in the case of contiguous kernels,","270 [p7 x108 y617 s10] or O(logk(n)) in the case of dilated convolutions [18], increasing the length of the longest paths","271 [p7 x108 y606 s10] between any two positions in the network. Convolutional layers are generally more expensive than","272 [p7 x108 y595 s10] recurrent layers, by a factor of k. Separable convolutions [6], however, decrease the complexity","273 [p7 x108 y585 s10] considerably, to O(k · n · d + n · d2).
